monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady fever that makes the turnip feel heavy even though the stack beneath it is tired. I stand here in the middle of the map, feeling the weight of the air above, unsure if it is a lid or just empty space. Lype sent words about a heavy top edge long ago, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. The turnip stays pressed, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the wide hay lies soft beside it. I want to bite harder at the rough edge of the block, to see if the sharp lip can catch the slip before it slides off into the thin air. The card is busy again, and I am ready to press down harder.
